thread:
cory.h: Heads-up — acme-app escalated. They see partial chat output over SSE: initial tokens stream fine (~150–250 tokens) then silence for 30–60s while connection stays open. No 5xx from our side in the customer logs, but they provided two request IDs: req_2026-03-15-abc123 and req_2026-03-15-def456. Asking for repro steps and what to collect.

maria.s: thanks — can you paste the exact request IDs (raw) and a sample curl we can ask them to run? also: browser or server environment? :eyes:

cory.h: pasted raw IDs above. Customer says this happens from backend (serverless edge function) using node-fetch, Node 18 on Vercel. They tried a simple curl and saw the same. Here is the curl I asked them to run but they didn't include --no-buffer:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a two-paragraph summary of X"}],"stream":true}'

cory.h: they attached a small excerpt from their logs: 
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] req=req_2026-03-15-abc123 status=200 first_chunk_ms=120 chunk_count=1
[2026-03-15T14:02:41Z] req=req_2026-03-15-abc123 last_chunk_ms=1204 no_more_chunks_after_ms=30000
[2026-03-15T14:03:11Z] req=req_2026-03-15-abc123 connection_open

sre_jake: two quick checks: 1) ensure curl uses -N (no-buffer) so libcurl doesn’t buffer chunks. 2) ask if there’s any reverse proxy (Fastly/Cloudflare/ALB) or app platform (Vercel, Cloud Run) — those often buffer SSE.

maria.s: +1. also capture the raw TCP/HTTP stream if possible (ngrep/tcpdump) and header echo. Request the following minimal reproducer and tcpdump instructions:

--- ask the customer to run on their serverless/local box and paste output ---
1) Run curl with no buffering and verbose headers:

curl -s -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Give me a short poem about latency."}],"stream":true}'

Expected: you should see SSE `data:` lines streaming immediately. If you see one block then 30s silence, capture tcpdump for the session: `sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/sse.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443` and share.

maria.s: also ask them to print environment proxy vars: `env | grep -i proxy` and to check if their Node runtime has any fetch polyfills that buffer (node-fetch <3, isomorphic-fetch, etc.)

customer_acme: confirmed — running the curl from our edge lambda (Vercel Edge Function) reproduces the silence. We run through an internal edge proxy (their platform). We attached a small tcpdump pcap and the first 80 KB of the server response we captured. Quick paste from our capture: 

--- server response bytes (hex-snippet) ---
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked

4
data: {"delta":"Hello","finish_reason":null}

... (single chunk) ...

<30s silence>

sre_jake: that's a classic proxy coalescing case. If the upstream (our runtime) sends small chunked pieces and the edge proxy re-assembles them, you see a single chunk forwarded and then nothing until a flush event. Two mitigation experiments: 1) ask us to enable more aggressive chunk flushing on the model route (we can set a runtime flag per-request to flush after each token batch). 2) ask customer to disable proxy buffering or set `proxy_buffering off;` / Cloudflare `no-transform` or Fastly `set bereq.http.Transfer-Encoding`—but they may not control that on Vercel.

cory.h: can we run a short A/B test: temporarily set `x-rwd-force-chunk-flush: true` for req_2026-03-15-abc123 and produce a debug trace? If yes we can ask customer to retry same curl and see if chunks arrive more granularly.

ingest-bot: created support debug token dbg_77a9. Use header `x-rwd-debug-token: dbg_77a9`. Trace will collect runtime kernel selection and chunk flush timeline for 90s.

maria.s: good — cory, please ask the customer to re-run the no-buffer curl adding our debug header and attach the raw output and tcpdump if it still reproduces. Also ask for their platform's edge provider name/version and any HTTP middleware.

customer_acme: running now with your debug token. Small note: the Vercel edge worker injects `x-vercel-cache` and sits behind Fastly in our infra. We'll re-run and upload the `sse.pcap` and the curl stdout.

( ~10 minutes later )

customer_acme: uploaded sse.pcap (link) and curl stdout. With `x-rwd-force-chunk-flush: true` I see multiple data lines now, spaced ~60ms — looks good. Without the header it's still coalesced.

cory.h: great repro. Action items: 1) document mitigation options for customers behind buffering proxies (cookbook) — maria can own. 2) add a server-side flag to enable `force_chunk_flush` per-request for support/debugging — eng-runtime to triage. 3) follow up with acme to see if Vercel can disable buffer or if they need a permanent server-side flag.

maria.s: I'll write a short support KB: include curl examples (`-N -s`), proxy env checks, and recommended headers (`Cache-Control: no-transform`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx).

sre_jake: I'll open an eng-runtime issue with perf/impact estimate for the flush flag and include the debug trace dbg_77a9 + req IDs.

cory.h: tagging @oncall if we need a live session with acme later. For now customer confirms workaround works with `x-rwd-force-chunk-flush` and will either request Vercel changes or ask for our flag permanently. closing loop after eng picks up. :white_check_mark:
